title: Keeping Good Conduct
note: This is keeping the conduct laid down for your varna and stage of life. It follows restraint because only those who have restrained body, speech and mind can do it.

couplets.plain: Conduct brings excellence, so guard your conduct more closely than your life.
couplets.pm: Conduct gives distinction to everyone, high and low alike, so it is to be guarded more than life. Life is the best of all things, but it doesn’t give distinction as conduct does.
couplets.sensitive: ranks conduct above one's own life; could reach someone in shame

links.quote: guard your conduct more closely than your life

couplets.plain: Guard your conduct with anxious care. Search and test as you will, it alone is your companion.
couplets.pm: Protect conduct, even with pain, letting none of it perish. Examine all kinds of righteousness, ask with a settled mind which helps in both worlds, and conduct is the one that proves your help. These two couplets tell the excellence of conduct.

couplets.plain: Good conduct is noble family. A lapse in it becomes low birth.
couplets.pm: For everyone, the conduct right for their varna is high family. Lapsing from it becomes a lower varna. Those of a low family within their varna become high by conduct. Those born in a high varna become low by lapsing. The result follows at once, so the deeds themselves are named as the results.
couplets.sensitive: uses low birth as a term of disgrace, plainly so in the Tamil

links.reason: Takes conduct as noble family, and a lapse in it as low birth.

couplets.plain: A Brahmin who forgets his scripture can learn it again. If his conduct falls, his birth is ruined.
couplets.pm: A Brahmin who forgets the Veda he learned can study it again, because his varna isn’t lost. But his high varna is lost when his conduct falls. “Forgets” is no licence, since forgetting too would lower him. This is said of the highest varna, and it holds for the others as well.

links.quote: If his conduct falls, his birth is ruined
links.reason: Sets it above scripture: what is forgotten can be learned again, a fall cannot.
The Brahmin is named, and his birth is what is at stake.

couplets.plain: Just as the envious have no gain, those without good conduct have no standing.
couplets.pm: As the envious have no gain, those without conduct have no height. From the comparison it follows that their kin have none either, because the kin of the envious go poor too. Height here means belonging to a high family.

links.quote: those without good conduct have no standing
links.reason: Denies any standing to those who lack it.

couplets.plain: The strong-minded don’t slacken in their conduct, for they know the harm that comes of a lapse.
couplets.pm: Those strong of mind don’t cut back on conduct because it is hard, for they know that a lapse brings them the fault of low family. They are called strong because they don’t give up the vow they have taken.

links.quote: The strong-minded don’t slacken in their conduct

couplets.plain: By good conduct people reach greatness. By a lapse they reach blame they didn’t deserve.
couplets.pm: Everyone reaches eminence by conduct. By falling from it they get blame they don’t deserve. When enemies bring a false charge, the world believes it because of the lapse. These five couplets tell the good of having conduct and the fault of lacking it.

links.quote: By a lapse they reach blame they didn’t deserve
links.reason: Sets greatness against the blame that comes to those who lapse.

couplets.plain: Good conduct is the seed of good. Bad conduct brings suffering always.
couplets.pm: Good conduct is the cause of righteousness and gives joy in both worlds. Bad conduct is the cause of sin and gives suffering in both. Naming one half of each implies the other. This tells what follows from conduct later.

links.reason: Sets it against bad conduct as the seed of good against the source of suffering.
Conduct is a seed, with good as its crop.

couplets.plain: Those with good conduct can’t say evil things with their mouths, even by a slip.
couplets.pm: Those with conduct can’t utter evil words with their mouths, even by forgetting. Evil words are lies and the like that harm others, and words not fit for their varna. “Mouths” is added to say their mouths are practised in good words.

links.reason: Those of good conduct can’t bring themselves to say evil things.

links.quote: can’t say evil things with their mouths
links.reason: Evil words do not pass their lips even by a slip.

couplets.plain: Those who don’t learn to move in step with the world may learn much, but they are still without understanding.
couplets.pm: Those who haven’t learned to live in accord with the world have no understanding, though they have read many books. To accord with the world is to live as the high-minded have lived. That drops what the law books say that no longer suits the time, and takes up what suits it though unsaid. The use of learning is knowledge, and the use of knowledge is conduct.

links.reason: Says that no amount of learning gives understanding to those out of step with the world.

links.quote: move in step with the world
links.reason: The failing is not moving in step with the world, which no book learning makes up for.
